reading: Output is 5x the input size in 3x3 blocks: the central 3x3 blocks show the input scaled by 3 (each fg cell a solid block), and each solid block on the edge of that core gets a copy of the input in the outer-ring block just beyond it (outward).

slots.core: input scaled x3 into blocks (1..3,1..3) of a 5x5 block grid
slots.sprout_at: outer-ring block adjacent (up/down/left/right, away from centre) to each solid core block lying on the core's edge

why: every output block is solid fg, the input, or empty; solid blocks = input fg cells shifted by (1,1); input copies sit exactly outward of edge-of-core solid blocks

reading: Each colour-4 shape stands against a straight vertical 2-segment, with one single marker cell of another colour on the other side; the shape is reflected across the 2-segment and the reflection is painted in the marker's colour.

slots.subject: each 4-shape attached to a 2-segment
slots.colour: colour of the single marker cell on the far side of that segment

why: the new cells are the mirror image of the 4-shape across its 2-segment, all in the marker colour (the marker cell lies inside the reflection or is kept)

reading: A 9 line runs along one border; each 8 lying inside a 2-area turns into 2, and each 8 lying inside the 7-area grows by one cell toward the 9 line (the neighbouring cell on the 9 side becomes 8).

slots.rule_in_7: cell one step toward the 9 border line becomes 8

why: only 8 cells and the cell next to a 7-area 8 on the 9 side change

reading: From each 6 on the bottom row a 2-path runs upward; when a horizontal 7-bar blocks it, the path marks the bar cell with 8, runs right under the bar (4 at the turn, 3 one past the bar end) and continues up past the bar's right end; it ends with a 6 at the top row or where it can no longer pass.

slots.path: 2 cells going up, detouring right under each bar
slots.marks: 8 on the bar cell above the path, 4 at the turn below it, 3 at the corner past the bar end
slots.end: 6 at the top row or when the detour is blocked

why: every new cell lies on a path from a bottom 6; 7 cells only change to 8 where a path meets them

reading: Four 4-cells mark the corners of the output box; inside it some blocks of a scaled-up copy of a small multicoloured template (found elsewhere in the grid) are shown; the output is the box cut out with the scaled template completed.

slots.box: rectangle with the four 4 corner markers
slots.template: small multicoloured component outside the box
slots.scale: factor making template cells match the partial blocks inside the box

why: output = box between the 4 corners, the 4s at its corners, and inside exactly the template scaled and placed over the existing partial blocks

reading: Each non-background colour has a square number of cells; the output draws one solid square per colour (side = sqrt of its count), bottom-aligned, ordered smallest to largest from left to right, separated by one background column.
why: output width = sum of sides + gaps, height = largest side; each square holds exactly its colour's count

reading: Each solid rectangle contains one odd-coloured cell; the rectangle keeps its border, its interior is cleared to background, and diagonals from the four interior corners are drawn inward in the odd colour, joining at the centre (by a short straight run when the interior is not square).

slots.subject: each solid rectangle
slots.colour: the single odd cell inside it
slots.pattern: X of diagonals from the interior corners, joined at the middle

why: only interior cells of rectangles change; each becomes either background or the odd colour on the corner diagonals

reading: Output is 3x the input in 3x3 blocks; block (i,j) holds the colour-inverted input (fg and background swapped) when input cell (i,j) is background, and is empty otherwise.
verb: tile inverted input at background cells

frame.verb: tile inverted input at background cells

slots.unit: input with its one fg colour and background swapped

why: every output block is either the inverted input or empty, and it is the inverted input exactly where the input cell is background

reading: Three 3x3 panels separated by 5 columns: the left panel stays, the middle panel becomes the left panel rotated 90 degrees clockwise, and the right panel becomes it rotated 180 degrees.
why: separators and left panel unchanged; panel k = left panel rotated by (k-1)*90 degrees clockwise

reading: The 8 shapes are drawn on a grid of 4x4 blocks (starting at the top-left fg cell); every background cell inside a block that contains 8 is filled with 2.

new_rows.name: blk_bg
new_rows.datalog:
y0(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
x0(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
rowb(Y, B) :- px(Y, 0, C), px(B, 0, C2), y0(A), L = A + 4 * B, H = L + 3, Y >= L, Y <= H.
colb(X, B) :- px(0, X, C), px(0, B, C2), x0(A), L = A + 4 * B, H = L + 3, X >= L, X <= H.
hasfg(BY, BX) :- cell(Y, X, C), rowb(Y, BY), colb(X, BX).
blk_bg(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C), rowb(Y, BY), colb(X, BX), hasfg(BY, BX).

why: every background cell in a 4x4 block (aligned to the fg top-left) that holds an 8 becomes 2; nothing else changes
